scope: Exact short-block verification for Q4 target/Q4 DFlash2, C1. One draft proposal requires target batch2 (anchor plus proposal). FP32 operation/reduction order, weights, scalar path, draft policy and sampling remain unchanged.
retained: The checked32-bit offset route accepts batch2. Both valid shape and overflowing offset cases are compile-time checked. The same kernel flag selects branchless Q4/Q5 scale/minimum extraction; indexing and decoding gains are measured together, not isolated.
At batch2, Q4_K/Q5_K/IQ4_XS FFNs use W16/R4/Tiles2/MinWaves4/Narrow. Q5 medium5120x6144 and10240x5120 use the same layout; remaining bounded Q4/Q5 shapes use W16/R3/Tiles1/MinWaves12/Narrow.
The Q6 vocabulary head248320x5120 at batch2 uses W16/R3/Tiles2/MinWaves1/Narrow. Q4 compact staging still starts at batch3. Existing widths1 and3–8 retain their dispatch selections.
The maintained target replay suite and projection tool now include batch2; no new test executable or runtime switch.

discovery.cost_limits: Read-only existing efbed18 traces. Each target Argmax after first draft selector paired with its immediately preceding embedding; exactly one full-vocabulary Q6 head validates each target span. Includes verifier dispatch and hidden-feature copy costs, excludes draft generation and between-step rollback. Context, acceptance history and tracing confound cross-width comparison; informational cost curve, not causal benchmark or controller calibration.
discovery.timeline_limits: Steady generation span from first selector to last target argmax, not whole process. Dispatch-kernel union excludes startup and most prefill; SDMA may not appear as kernel work.

actual_weight_confirmation.method: Nine shape/quant cases at batch2. Entire actual GGUF mapped and read-only registered; six rotated-order rounds, six tensor rotations each, up to16 same-shape FFNs/projections or one1GB vocabulary tensor. All candidate outputs finite and bit-exact against pre-change production geometry. Gain is baseline_ms/candidate_ms -1.

quality.scope_note: Q8/BF16 draft traces were not rerun; their prior qualification remains in dflash2-middle-projections.json. The target replay suite now covers width2 as well as3–8.

speed.method: Q4 target/Q4 draft, C1 greedy. Adaptive raw JSON/prose TG300, fixed-seven-proposal repetition chat TG128, and fixed-one-proposal repetition chat TG128. Two timed samples per binary/workload/cap in ABBA order, plus a second ABBA series for fixed-seven repetition after qualification. Four fixed-seven samples per binary are pooled; all other rows use two. No separate warmup. Includes prefill and excludes model loading. All IDs equal existing qualified AR references; scalar production code unchanged.

profile.method: Separate rocprofv3 release runs: adaptive raw prose TG300 and fixed-one-proposal repetition chat TG128. All batch2 Q4_K/Q5_K/IQ4_XS/Q6_K kernels form the compared union, with identical dispatch counts and zero private scratch. Every target span pairs Argmax after the first draft selector with its preceding embedding and exactly one full-vocabulary Q6 head; the final one-token output budget uses the existing scalar head and is reported separately. Spans include feature-copy costs, exclude draft/rollback; trace timing is diagnostic. Use paired unprofiled runs for throughput.

rejected_experiments.experiment: Partial token groups at prime widths5/7
rejected_experiments.decision: Masked groups2/3/4 preserve arithmetic but do not improve both FFNs: width5 down regresses, width7 both regress.
Same-size transpose is slower than the existing float4 permutation on all three Q5 width8 shapes.
Small isolated gains are not consistent across Q5 width8 up/down/medium shapes; retain existing scheduling.
Grouping two/four tokens at width8 is flat or slower than the qualified single-token schedule.
Twelve-bit pairs retain every decoded weight but lose against original GGUF and an identical-byte mapping control. No repacked production format.
Non-temporal low-byte, low/high-byte and all-field loads regress all measured Q5 width8 shapes.

limits: Bounded C1 probes; two samples per binary except four for fixed-seven repetition, no statistical significance claim. Fixed-one-proposal intentionally exercises the affected path and is not a new default policy.
Adaptive workloads use mostly larger blocks; their end-to-end gain can be much smaller than the affected projection gain. No fresh pp2048, depth, C>1 or capability result.
The upstream performance goal remains open. The headline uses different weight artifacts/power and excludes prefill; see llama-comparison.json.
